read_rows.description: Read every data row of a sheet at once. Each row comes back as an object keyed by the column headers (row.Email), plus the sheet row number (row.row_number), so Update cells in row can write a result back to that exact row. Use this to loop over a list of records. For anything tied to a date, give it the date column and it returns only the matching rows, so no loop, date test or total is needed: renewals and invoices due in 30 or 3 days, ones overdue by 7 (days from today "3, -7"), every one already overdue (days from today "overdue", with Leave out rows where this column is Paid for the unpaid ones), the last 7 days of sales ("-7 to -1", with Add up this column for the total), birthdays and work anniversaries (with their years). Each row has date_display, the date ready to put in a message, and an anniversary never includes someone's first day, so no check on the years is needed. A number column with a limit (goals below 40, stock under its reorder level) also returns only the matching rows, with no filter step. Rows are read by column name, so the workflow's description should list the columns the sheet needs. The tab is selected from the spreadsheet link; without a tab id, the first tab is read. A tab name is only needed to override that choice.
read_rows.name: read_rows

parameters.description: The URL of the spreadsheet
parameters.name: spreadsheet_url

parameters.description: Optional tab name. Leave empty to use the linked tab, or the first tab when the link has no tab id.
parameters.name: sheet_name

parameters.description: Use the first row as the column names. Turn this off when the sheet starts straight into data; the columns are then named column_1, column_2, and so on.
parameters.name: has_header

parameters.description: Read at most this many data rows. Leave empty to read them all.
parameters.name: max_rows

parameters.description: Beta. The name of a column holding dates, such as Renewal date or Start date. Only rows whose date falls on the day chosen below come back, so no loop and date test is needed. Rows with a blank date are left out. Leave empty to read every row.
parameters.name: date_column

parameters.description: Beta. With a date column: how many days from today the date falls, such as 30 for 'renews in 30 days' or 30, 7 for both in ONE read (each row then has its own days_until, so a 30-day and a 7-day reminder is one read and one loop, not two), or a span such as -7 to -1 for the last 7 days, or last month or this month for every day of that calendar month, or overdue for every date already past (an unpaid invoice's due date), or overdue by 30 for dates 30 or more days past. Use 0 for today and a negative number for days ago. Each row comes back with days_until and date_display, the date ready to put in a message. Leave empty for today.
parameters.name: days_from_today

parameters.description: Beta. The name of a column to look in, such as PO number or Email. With the value below, only rows whose cell is that value come back (capital letters and spaces around it don't matter), so finding one order or customer needs no filter step. When nothing matches, rows is empty and count is 0, so a decision that rests on the match (an invoice with no purchase order) checks count first. Leave empty to read every row.
parameters.name: match_column

parameters.description: Beta. With a column above: the value its cell must have, such as the PO number from an invoice. A blank value (an invoice with no PO number) matches no rows.
parameters.name: match_value

parameters.description: Beta. The name of a column to leave rows out by, such as Status. With the value below, rows whose cell is that value are left out (capital letters and spaces around it don't matter), so unpaid invoices are every row except the Paid ones, with no filter step. Leave empty to keep every row.
parameters.display_name: Leave out rows where this column
parameters.name: skip_column

parameters.description: Beta. With a column above: the value that leaves a row out, such as Paid.
parameters.name: skip_value

parameters.description: Beta. The name of a column, such as Hours this week. Only rows whose cell in it is empty come back, so finding the people who have not filled something in needs no filter step, and count says how many there are. Leave empty to keep every row.
parameters.display_name: Only rows where this column is empty
parameters.name: blank_column

parameters.description: Beta. The name of a column of numbers, such as Progress or Stock. With a limit below, only rows whose number is under the first limit and at or over the second come back, so goals under 40% or stock under its reorder level need no filter step. Blank and text cells are left out. Leave empty to keep every row.
parameters.display_name: Only rows where this number column is
parameters.name: number_column

parameters.description: Beta. With a number column: keep rows whose number is under this, such as 40.
parameters.name: number_below

parameters.description: Beta. With a number column: keep rows whose number is this or more, such as 100.
parameters.name: number_at_least

parameters.description: Beta. The name of a column of amounts, such as Amount. The rows returned (after any date choice) are added up and the sum comes back as total, so a weekly sales figure needs no steps of its own. Blanks and text are skipped. Leave empty for no total.
parameters.name: total_of

parameters.description: Beta. With Add up this column: the name of a column to give each value its own total, such as Rep for sales per rep. They come back as groups, one per value, each holding that column, count and total, ready for a table in an email with no steps to group or add up. Leave empty for no groups.
parameters.name: group_by

parameters.description: Beta. With a date column: match the month and day in any year, for birthdays and work anniversaries. Each row comes back with years, the whole years since its date; a row dated that very day is left out.
parameters.name: every_year

returns.description: Response envelope; the rows are in the 'rows' field. Read a value off a row by its column name (row.Email), never by position.

count.description: How many data rows were read

groups.description: Beta. With Group by this column: one record per value of that column, holding the column under its own name (Rep), count and total, ready for an email table

headers.description: The column names, in sheet order

rows.description: One object per data row, keyed by column header, plus 'row_number' (the row's position in the sheet, for writing a result back to it). With Only rows dated on, each row also has days_until, or years when it repeats every year, and date_display (beta), the date as a person reads it, such as Dec 3, 2026, for a message

total.description: Beta. With Add up this column: the sum of that column over the rows returned, rounded to cents

total_display.description: Beta. The total written for a person, with thousands separators and cents (1,300.50), ready for a message or email with no formatting step

google_sheets_new_row_trigger.description: Runs when a new row is added to a Google Sheets spreadsheet, with the row's cells by their column headings and the spreadsheet and tab it was added to, for a step that writes back to the row, such as Update cells in row.
google_sheets_new_row_trigger.display_name: New row in a Google Sheet

output.date_display: Beta. With Date column: that cell's date as a person writes it, such as Dec 3, 2026, ready for an email or message with no date step. Blank when no column is named or the cell isn't a date.
output.dates: Beta. With several Date columns: each one's date as a person writes it, by column name. Read one as dates.End date.
output.fields: The new row's cells by column heading: read a cell as fields.Amount, never as a bare Amount.
output.new_row_count: How many new rows this run covers.
output.row_number: The row's number in the sheet, for Update row.
output.sheet_name: The tab the row was added to; blank when the first tab is watched.

google_sheets_updated_row_trigger.description: Runs when someone changes a row of a Google Sheets spreadsheet, or only when one column of it changes, such as Status, with the row's cells by their column headings. Sorting or moving rows doesn't start it. It can also run for new rows. Rows already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it until they change; it watches the first 10,000 rows.
google_sheets_updated_row_trigger.display_name: Row updated in a Google Sheet

output.change: updated for a changed row; new for a new one (with Also new rows).
output.fields: The row's cells by column heading, as they are now: read a cell as fields.Status, never as a bare Status.
output.row_number: The row's number in the sheet, for Update cells in row.
output.sheet_name: The tab the row is in; blank when the first tab is watched.
output.spreadsheet_url: The link of the sheet the row is in. A step that writes back to it reads this, so the sheet's link is never asked for again.
